t: A week after being arrested by the Prussian Secret Police, French police inspector Guillaume Schnaebelé was released on the order of William I, German Emperor, defusing a possible war.
The Parliament of Canada passed the Rocky Mountains Park Act, creating Banff National Park in Alberta as the country's first national park.
L. L. Zamenhof published Unua Libro, the first publication to describe Esperanto, a constructed international language.
A fire that killed 186 people broke out at the Theatre Royal, Exeter, England.
Johannes Brahms conducted the premiere of his Double Concerto, composed for violinist Joseph Joachim and cellist Robert Hausmann.
